supporting_observations.claim: WS-LMARTINS-01 repeatedly made proxy CONNECT requests to updates.pixelforge-suite.co at roughly five-minute intervals from 13:37:36 through 14:07:36 UTC. The inventory lists the approved PixelForge update domain as updates.pixelforge-suite.com, which is different from the observed .co hostname.

The process making the recurring connections was pfupdater.exe running from Leo Martins's AppData\Roaming\PixelForge directory, rather than the inventory's approved C:\Program Files\PixelForge\pfupdater.exe location. Its recorded parent was Explorer and it ran at Medium integrity.

Sysmon recorded pfupdater.exe creating a file at its own executable path shortly after it started. This is unusual in combination with the non-approved path and mismatched update hostname, though the record alone does not establish what changed.
The recurring proxy connections are attributed by endpoint network telemetry to process ID 3992, the same AppData\Roaming pfupdater.exe process, connecting to the explicit proxy on port 8080.

Dropbox and Google Drive File Stream processes also started in Leo Martins's user session. The inventory does not approve these file-sharing services; these records establish process starts, not that either service transferred data.

known_telemetry_limitations: The suspicious HTTPS activity is recorded as proxy CONNECT tunnels; the supplied records do not expose the tunneled application payload. Relevant examples include T045-00089, T045-00112, and T045-00235.
The supplied records do not include a hash, signature validation, or file contents for the AppData\Roaming pfupdater.exe; T045-00087 and T045-00093 identify its path and a file-creation event only.
claims_not_established: The records do not establish who controls updates.pixelforge-suite.co or whether its content was malicious.
The records do not establish what data, if any, was sent or received in the encrypted tunnels, or whether data was exfiltrated.
The records do not establish what file contents changed during the pfupdater.exe file-creation event or whether a payload was downloaded and executed.
The records do not establish that Dropbox or Google Drive File Stream transferred data during the review window.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and preserve the pfupdater.exe file and related files from the AppData\Roaming\PixelForge directory; calculate hashes and verify signatures against the vendor's approved updater.
Review proxy and TLS inspection records, DNS and certificate details, and vendor confirmation for updates.pixelforge-suite.co and the observed sessions.
Collect endpoint file, process, persistence, and download telemetry around the updater's start and file-creation event.
Review file-access and cloud-sync activity for Dropbox, Google Drive, and OneDrive to determine whether data was accessed or transferred.
